title: least-privilege mapper and audit timestamping proxy
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: tighten operator and service privileges at the decision boundary and make audit events deterministic across region-pin and KMS fallbacks. This PR implements a compact least-privilege mapper that translates high-level role templates into explicit action/resource allowlists, plus an audit timestamping proxy that canonicalizes audit headers (tenant, geozone-hash, and operation-time) before events hit the ingestion pipeline. Key benefits: (1) avoids on-path attribute expansion that created noisy decision graphs and accidental privilege escalation, (2) stamps a stable audit timestamp and tenant-geozone fingerprint to aid downstream reconciliation when KMS or region-fallbacks occur, and (3) exposes a small, testable policy translation surface to enable safer RBAC v2 rollouts. What changed: added pkg/auth/min_privilege_mapper.go implementing attribute-driven allowlist generation; added pkg/audit/timestamping_proxy.go which normalizes and signs audit headers using the existing signing key (with a feature flag to switch to CMK-backed signing); added policy templates under configs/policies/min_privilege/*.yaml; added integration tests in ci/e2e/privilege_mapper_test.go exercising cross-region requests and KMS fallback paths; added migration docs and a conservative rollout plan under docs/security/min-privilege-mapper.md. Rollout plan: feature-flag behind ff/security.min_privilege_mapper; staged canary to 5% tenant traffic for 48 hours with telemetry gating; enable audit timestamping in read-only mode for 1 week then opt-in signing; full rollout only after no regression in auth-failure rate and latency budgets. Backwards compatibility: the mapper emits allowlists but preserves existing policy decision hooks; proxy can be run in pass-through mode. KMS interaction: when CMK signing is unavailable due to residency constraints, proxy will fall back to HSM-backed local signing and annotate events with kms_fallback=true. Observability: added metrics rbac.mapper.rules_generated, audit.proxy.fallback_count, audit.proxy.sign_latency_ms and traces for the translation path. Security review: built with threat-model mitigations to avoid leaking tenant region claims to operator logs (attribute suppression enabled by default). Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration e2e tests [x] docs [x] migration notes [x] security review sign-off. Related: ENG-8421 (rbac rollout), SEC-214 (audit determinism), SUP-1023 (customer report about cross-region audit deltas).

release_notes: Adds a conservative least-privilege translation layer and an audit timestamping proxy. Improves deterministic audit events across region pinning and KMS fallbacks. Feature gated and rolled out incrementally.
migration_steps: Enable ff/security.min_privilege_mapper in canary for 5% of tenants
Run audit proxy in read-only stamping mode for 1 week to validate fields
Monitor rbac.mapper.rules_generated and auth failure rates, revert if spikes
Enable CMK signing for proxy once tenancy residency checks pass
Flip ff/security.min_privilege_mapper to on for all tenants
testing_notes: Added deterministic e2e scenario that replays a tenant request with and without region pin to validate audit header parity
Manual test: simulate CMK unavailable -> proxy should set kms_fallback=true and still emit signed event using local HSM
Performance: local canary showed median proxy latency +0.9ms p95 +3.4ms under load; plan includes micro-optimizations if we see degradation in Dedicated tiers
